Review.Independence: An independent reviewer that took no part in preparing or implementing this change and was given no authoring conversation. It read the contract of revision 2, brief-1 and brief-2, approval-1 and approval-2, the receipts of runs 1 to 3 with their logs, the four cited rule files, and the complete source diff from c49bf8944d0d93894151671257f0c95763110c78 to f262634a1f96b040d8212bb189d05ef36880584d. It recomputed independently the contract hash (e9d1f92c0bcdca6abcc9453415280e400d15415092f6f83fca956726a5873e35), the brief-2 hash (e5732a46c731db81a14ce667200f35dfcfa913a5d496bf8f4c5df4a06538f0c0), the five bound definition hashes that check reports, the candidate of HEAD (ec040ca0d3f9b441dba29303dae1446e8ce5aa1119ce4dd9ed59f99676be8cc2), the dirty path list (empty) and the changed-path list of the complete diff; it hashed every run-3 log against its receipt; it ran all five checks itself on the final revision; it exercised the guard outside the repository in scratch fixtures for unstaged, staged, untracked and renamed skill paths, a .git file (worktree), a missing .git, a checkout nested in a parent repository, a deleted and a missing packages/skills tree, a non-ASCII path, a sibling directory that must not match, and upgrade with plan true and false against a dirty and a clean kernel source; and it compared the approval brief hashes of the closed changes against their committed blobs with git cat-file. It edited nothing but this record.

Finding.Text: UP-20 is the only test of the guard, and it discriminates less than brief-2 and the conformance.md UP-20 row claim. It dirties one unstaged file, packages/skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md, and asserts one refusal naming that path, exit 1, no plan line, and the pin still at 0.5.0; it then shows a bump-only chain on the same dirty source succeeding and writing the pin, and a clean fixture kernel upgrading and refreshing. What it does not discriminate: (a) plan mode - no test passes plan: true with a dirty kernelRoot, so A1's "with and without --plan" clause rests on reading the code, and I could only confirm the behaviour by calling applyUpgrade({plan: true}) against a dirty fixture kernel myself (exit 1, one refusal, no printed lines, pin unchanged) and against a clean one (plan printed, exit 0); (b) the canonical skills/ tree - no test dirties it, so deleting "skills" from SKILL_SOURCES would leave the suite green although D1 covers both trees; (c) staged, untracked and renamed skill paths, which I confirmed only in scratch fixtures; (d) a kernelRoot without .git, never passed; (e) the installed skill bytes, which the refusal leaves untouched but which the test does not assert, checking only the pin; (f) the link between kernelRoot and packagedSkills, since the clean upgrade reads PACKAGED_SKILLS from the real kernel while the guard inspects a different fixture tree, so the test cannot show that the guard watches the tree the refresh actually reads - which is what the shared default KERNEL_ROOT gives in production. brief-2's CK2 row nonetheless states that the suite shows the refusal "with and without --plan", and conformance.md UP-20 states the no-.git case that no test exercises. The behaviour itself is correct as read and as exercised; the claim about what the suite proves is not. The remedy is one cheap test with plan: true on a dirty kernel and one passing a .git-less kernelRoot, and a dirty canonical skills/ path.

The refusal appends a sentence the documents do not state: the command emits "kernel skills are modified relative to HEAD: <path> (commit them or run from a released commit)", while upgrade.md gives the line as "kernel skills are modified relative to HEAD: <path>, <path>" and the help's Output block as "kernel skills are modified relative to HEAD: <path>", both ending at the path list. A path list followed by prose inside the same comma-separated field is also not what "naming each modified path" describes, and a reader or script that takes the field after the colon as the path list now gets one path with advice glued to it. The fixed phrase still matches, so no check and no reader who greps is harmed, and the advice is useful; the deviation is documentary and small. Verified by running applyUpgrade with plan true and plan false against a dirty fixture kernel.

The pin changes the bytes a checkout materialises, and two closed approvals bind a brief hash over CRLF bytes. C-0007-orchestrate-skill approval-5 records brief-sha256 39ec5dcf23796edb6df11161ae506f174db62264747dcc928c38e1efb39ba63d, which equals the current CRLF worktree copy of records/brief-5.html (25536 bytes) and not the committed blob (25352 bytes, 0699b8e8959a50e464e75c5c36782da12d13e3a778016d5bae2afacde17a3feb). C-0010-parallel-conformance approval-1 records f5cb3173e2e585158b72983d79225faabf4af17d0e9de95fe4e17582657ac4bd, which equals its CRLF worktree copy (17153 bytes) and not the committed blob (16966 bytes, c5926367d9ba8848698bbab4a8292d098b0dfec8bf3d17f1880f7d4924410b8b). This worktree still matches because git never rewrites a file it considers clean: 12 tracked files under .grace5/changes/closed/ are i/lf w/crlf today. A fresh clone now always writes LF, so those two briefs hash to the LF values and the recorded hashes stop reproducing for any reader who hashes the checkout - the very machines the pin targets (the Problem cites a clone with core.autocrlf=true) now disagree with the record. Nothing in the kernel re-reads a closed change's brief: status reports "next: none, the change is closed" and check reports no defect for both changes on a CRLF and on an LF copy, so no evidence is invalidated and this is a documentary consequence, not a defect to fix by rewriting a record - rewriting the briefs would falsify them. But the Change and D6 say the pin "alters no record", which is literally true and reads as "no record is affected", and two are. The asymmetry is in the rules, not the pin: authorization.md reads CRLF as LF for the contract hash and binds a brief over raw bytes, so only briefs are exposed. Either sentence of the contract should say this, or a later change should normalise the brief hash rule.

The guard treats "no answer from git" as "clean". modifiedSkillSources returns an empty list when .git is absent, which D4 states, and also when spawnSync yields a non-zero status or no status at all: git missing from PATH, a .git file whose gitdir is gone, a repository git refuses to read (dubious ownership), or a status output above the 16 MiB maxBuffer. In each case the upgrade refreshes installed skills from a working tree nobody verified, and nothing says so. The kernel uses the same convention in git.ts dirtyPaths, so the choice is consistent rather than novel, and it is the right default for a checkout that is not a checkout; what is missing is that the contract's D4 names only the absent .git while the code also covers an unreadable one. The same filter makes a kernel checkout nested inside a parent worktree trusted, because the test is the presence of .git at the root rather than openGit's answer; the approved text covers that case as written, but the guard is then off for a vendored checkout while git could have answered. No test reaches any of these paths. A one-line mention in upgrade.md next to the no-.git exclusion, or an explicit failure instead of an empty list when .git exists and git cannot answer, would close it.

Review.Adequacy: bun run check is tsc --noEmit over the whole kernel, and I reran it on f262634a1f96b040d8212bb189d05ef36880584d: exit 0. It discriminates the failure it claims and the brief attributes to it: a new module that does not type-check, a wrong optional parameter or import in chain.ts, a broken fixture type in the new test, or an unused import would fail the build. It exercises no behaviour at all: it cannot show that the guard fires, that the refusal precedes the plan, that the exit status is 1, that the paths are named, or that .gitattributes exists, none of which it reads; that is CK2's and CK4's and CK5's work.

bun test --parallel, rerun by the review on the final revision: 95 pass, 1 skip (the POSIX-only signal test), 0 fail, 1445 expect() calls across 12 files, matching the run-3 log whose hash the receipt carries. The suite discriminates the guard's core failure modes through UP-20: delete the guard and the refusal assertion, the exit status, the empty line list and the unchanged pin all fail; print the plan before the refusal and the empty line list fails; consult the source for a bump-only chain and the bump case fails; refuse a clean source and the clean case fails. The test builds a real git fixture kernel, so the git status call, the pathspec over both trees and the path naming are exercised rather than mocked. It does not discriminate plan mode, the canonical skills/ tree, staged, untracked or renamed skill paths, a .git-less kernelRoot, the installed-skill bytes after a refusal, or the coupling of kernelRoot to the skills the refresh installs (F1); those rest on my reading and on the scratch fixtures I ran. It also says nothing about whether the help, upgrade.md, commands.md and conformance.md agree with each other or with the code; that is reading, and F2 is where they disagree.

bun run package:verify regenerates the packaged skills and models/architecture/cli-reference.md from their sources and fails on any drift; I reran it on the final revision and all four checks reported ok (claude-plugin, openpackage, skills, cli-reference). It discriminates A4's generated-output clause: the new help paragraph and the new Output line reach cli-reference.md or the run fails, and no installed skill byte or generated package moved. It does not discriminate the behaviour, the wording's intent, or .gitattributes: a misleading help sentence would be copied faithfully and pass, and it reads neither the attribute file nor the index, so A3 rests on CK4 and on the premise the contract states.

git check-attr eol over skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md and packages/skills/grace5-prepare/SKILL.md, rerun by the review with both expected lines in order and exit 0. It discriminates A3's attribute clause: without the committed .gitattributes rule git answers "unspecified" and the expected markers are absent. It does not discriminate A3's second clause, "the index has no CRLF blob", which it never reads; I verified that separately with git ls-files --eol (237 tracked entries, none i/crlf or i/mixed, and 12 i/lf w/crlf files, all under .grace5/changes/closed/), and that verification is review work, not the check. Two sample files stand in for two whole trees, so a path-specific exception inside either tree would not be seen, and the receipt's origin is "any", recorded as marker-sequence-unattributed, so the pass claims only that the two lines appeared in the recorded output, not that they came from this checkout.

bun src/cli.ts upgrade --help, rerun by the review: the line "kernel skills are modified relative to HEAD" is present exactly once and the command exits 0. It discriminates A4's help clause: remove the paragraph or the Output line and the marker is absent. It reads help text, not the refusal: it cannot show that a real upgrade prints the sentence, names the paths, keeps the plan unprinted or exits 1, and no check reads upgrade.md or commands.md, so the documents' agreement with the help and the code is held by reading and by package:verify for the generated reference. Origin "any" makes the pass marker-sequence-unattributed: it claims the marker appeared in the recorded output and says nothing about where it was produced.
Review.Rule: The surface grows by nothing: no command, flag, schema, record kind or skill is added, and the one new mechanism, the guard, is the mechanism the contract's K1 names and it carries ledger entry L-26, as the standing rule requires. The Problem cites an explicit owner decision of 2026-11-16 and two observed failures, which is what a new mechanism needs. The documents are edited in place, one topic per file and one paragraph or list item per physical line (the commands.md bullet, the conformance.md row, the ledger row and the upgrade.md paragraph are each a single line). Generated output follows the repository rule: the help text was edited and models/architecture/cli-reference.md regenerated, and package:verify confirms it. Release identity is untouched: the diff holds no package.json, no .grace5/kernel-version, no README status line and no STEPS row. Whether the mechanical work was delegated cannot be read from a diff, and I claim nothing about it.

Every requirement this document states for the change is met. The refusal is documented in the command section with its condition, the pin-bump exclusion, the no-.git exclusion and its place before the plan and before anything is written, with or without --plan; the migration table, the local ignore file and the two kinds of write are unchanged; no boundary or row is registered and the version, pin and tag are untouched, which is K2. The implementation refuses only when the composed chain holds a step, before the plan loop and before the loop that writes, as UP-20 and my own plan-mode fixtures show. The one thing the implementation adds that the document does not state is the trailing sentence of the refusal, reported non-blocking as F2; it changes none of the condition, order or effect the document describes.

The guard reads and writes nothing outside the kernel checkout it inspects; its only effect is to return 1 before the plan. No kernel-managed path is in the complete diff: the change's own contract and records under .grace5/ are excluded by path, and the source diff is 11 files, each inside the contract's Affected list and none matching a Protected path, recomputed by the review with changedBetween and the contract's own lists. HEAD f262634a is clean - dirtyPaths returns an empty list with this change's records present - and the candidate computed by the documented rule is ec040ca0d3f9b441dba29303dae1446e8ce5aa1119ce4dd9ed59f99676be8cc2, the candidate on run-3. The installed skills, the pin and the packaged tree are untouched, so no candidate, dirty state, diff or evidence changes, which is K3.

One mechanism enters the ledger and it carries every field the rule requires: L-26 names the guard with its source (an explicit owner requirement of 2026-11-16 plus an observed failure), the smallest alternative (document the habit and check nothing), the expected benefit, the cost (one git status when the chain has a step, commit-before-upgrade, the two accepted residuals) and a removal criterion (the installation design seeds from a packaged artifact with content hashes, or the canonical tree becomes the released tree and a tag check replaces this one). Nothing else enters: .gitattributes is repository configuration rather than a kernel mechanism, as K4 states, and adds no entry.
